cyberpunk.rule.vehicle-repair.cost_or_limit: Minor damage: DV9 and 3 hours; major damage: DV13 and 1 day; destroyed: DV17 and 1 week.
cyberpunk.rule.vehicle-repair.go_wrong: A failed roll means the repair must be restarted halfway through.
cyberpunk.rule.vehicle-repair.who_may: Characters using an applicable TECH skill
cyberpunk.rule.vehicle-repair.blocked_reason: It is a game procedure for resolving repairs, not a world mechanism.

cyberpunk.rule.item-repair.name: Item Repair

effect.summary: none stated

cyberpunk.rule.item-repair.cost_or_limit: Cheap/Everyday: DV9, 1 hour; Costly: DV13, 6 hours; Premium: DV17, 1 day; Expensive: DV21, 1 week; Very Expensive: DV24, 2 weeks; Luxury: DV29, 1 month; Super Luxury: DV29, 1 month per 10,000eb of price.
cyberpunk.rule.item-repair.go_wrong: A failed roll means the repair must be restarted halfway through.
cyberpunk.rule.item-repair.who_may: Characters using an applicable TECH skill
cyberpunk.rule.item-repair.blocked_reason: It is a game procedure for resolving repairs, not a world mechanism.

cyberpunk.rule.rumors-are-incomplete-and.name: Rumors are incomplete and potentially false

effect.summary: A rumor may be untrue and never presents the complete story.

cyberpunk.rule.rumors-are-incomplete-and.go_wrong: Treating a rumor as the full truth may mislead an investigation.
cyberpunk.rule.rumors-are-incomplete-and.blocked_reason: This is a usable informational constraint.

cyberpunk.rule.one-story-per-exact-topic.name: One story per exact topic

effect.summary: A Media cannot publish again on the same exact topic without new information.

cyberpunk.rule.one-story-per-exact-topic.cost_or_limit: New information is required for another publication on that topic.
cyberpunk.rule.one-story-per-exact-topic.blocked_reason: This is a clear restriction on repeated use.

cyberpunk.rule.team-member-loyalty-save.name: Team Member Loyalty Save

effect.summary: A d6 roll must be below a Team Member’s current Loyalty for the assigned task to proceed reliably.

cyberpunk.rule.team-member-loyalty-save.cost_or_limit: Failure may cause refusal, botching, or turning against the Exec; Loyalty at zero or lower prompts active betrayal.
cyberpunk.rule.team-member-loyalty-save.go_wrong: Loyalty below zero at session end leads the member to complain to HR and then transfer or quit.
cyberpunk.rule.team-member-loyalty-save.mind: Team Members have independent motives and are not mindless.
cyberpunk.rule.team-member-loyalty-save.who_may: Team Members responding to an Exec’s orders
cyberpunk.rule.team-member-loyalty-save.combines: Loyalty changes with conduct and can exceed its between-session cap during a session.
cyberpunk.rule.team-member-loyalty-save.blocked_reason: Task response depends on an NPC’s mental loyalty and possible betrayal.

cyberpunk.rule.team-member-replacement.name: Team Member replacement

effect.summary: HR repossesses a lost Team Member’s equipment and supplies a new hire next session.

cyberpunk.rule.team-member-replacement.cost_or_limit: The replacement has new stats, starts at Loyalty 1, and costs the Exec 200eb.
cyberpunk.rule.team-member-replacement.go_wrong: The replacement has reduced loyalty because they heard about the loss.
cyberpunk.rule.team-member-replacement.mind: The new hire’s starting attitude is affected by the prior incident.
cyberpunk.rule.team-member-replacement.who_may: Execs who lose a Team Member
cyberpunk.rule.team-member-replacement.blocked_reason: This is a straightforward replacement rule.

cyberpunk.rule.backup-call-response.name: Backup call response

effect.summary: A successful call brings backup after a d6 roll of rounds; a six upgrades the response, or adds a second group at rank 10.

cyberpunk.rule.backup-call-response.cost_or_limit: Calling costs an Action and requires a d10 result at or below rank; failed responses can be retried next turn.
cyberpunk.rule.backup-call-response.go_wrong: Excessive use can bring a fine or removal from the force.
cyberpunk.rule.backup-call-response.mind: A responder must choose to answer the call.
cyberpunk.rule.backup-call-response.combines: Response rank depends on the caller’s rank and the arrival roll.
cyberpunk.rule.backup-call-response.blocked_reason: The timing and response are modeled with ordinary checks and delayed arrivals.

cyberpunk.rule.rank-10-backup-follow-up.name: Rank 10 Backup follow-up

effect.summary: The same rank 10 responders investigate connected calls until the case closes or they fall in duty.

cyberpunk.rule.rank-10-backup-follow-up.cost_or_limit: They do not travel with the Crew day to day.
cyberpunk.rule.rank-10-backup-follow-up.go_wrong: They may fall in the line of duty.
cyberpunk.rule.rank-10-backup-follow-up.combines: Applies after the first call connected to the case.
cyberpunk.rule.rank-10-backup-follow-up.blocked_reason: The rule tracks a continuing NPC obligation.

cyberpunk.rule.family-vehicle-availabili.name: Family Vehicle availability

effect.summary: A Nomad normally has only one Family Vehicle out at a time; a nearby Family can swap it the next morning.

cyberpunk.rule.family-vehicle-availabili.cost_or_limit: At rank 10, the Nomad may have all Family Vehicles out at once.
cyberpunk.rule.family-vehicle-availabili.combines: A swap requires the Family to be nearby.
cyberpunk.rule.family-vehicle-availabili.mechanism: Vehicle access limit and delayed exchange
cyberpunk.rule.family-vehicle-availabili.blocked_reason: This is an explicit vehicle-access limit.

cyberpunk.rule.family-vehicle-repair.name: Family Vehicle repair

effect.summary: The Family repairs a destroyed Family Vehicle in one week for 500eb.

cyberpunk.rule.family-vehicle-repair.cost_or_limit: Daily repairs, such as removing bullets, remain the Nomad’s responsibility; the fee may be waived if broke, at reputational cost.
cyberpunk.rule.family-vehicle-repair.go_wrong: Failure to pay or upkeep can affect reputation as described.
cyberpunk.rule.family-vehicle-repair.blocked_reason: This is a straightforward repair and cost rule.

cyberpunk.rule.rank-10-family-leadership.name: Rank 10 Family leadership

effect.summary: At Moto rank 10, the Nomad leads the Family and may have all Family Vehicles out.

cyberpunk.rule.rank-10-family-leadership.cost_or_limit: Future vehicles cost market price and future upgrades cost 1,000eb each.
cyberpunk.rule.rank-10-family-leadership.combines: Changes access to Family Motorpool vehicles.
cyberpunk.rule.rank-10-family-leadership.blocked_reason: The rule changes resource access and adds a stated responsibility.

cyberpunk.rule.combat-turns-and-rounds.name: Combat turns and rounds

effect.summary: A turn and a round each take approximately three seconds; participants act in Initiative Queue order.

cyberpunk.rule.combat-turns-and-rounds.cost_or_limit: Initiative is REF plus 1d10; ties are rerolled.
cyberpunk.rule.combat-turns-and-rounds.combines: Each turn gives one Move Action and one other Action.
cyberpunk.rule.combat-turns-and-rounds.blocked_reason: This is a game procedure, not a world mechanism.

cyberpunk.rule.move-action-distance.name: Move Action distance

effect.summary: A character moves up to twice MOVE in metres/yards, or MOVE grid squares, per Move Action.

cyberpunk.rule.move-action-distance.cost_or_limit: Swimming, climbing, and running-start jumps cost twice the movement distance; standing jumps cover half the running-start distance.
cyberpunk.rule.move-action-distance.combines: Movement may be split around an Action.
cyberpunk.rule.move-action-distance.blocked_reason: This is a game procedure, not a world mechanism.

cyberpunk.rule.aimed-shots.name: Aimed Shots

effect.summary: A one-rate-of-fire attack can target the head, a held item, or a leg at a -8 check penalty for additional effects.

cyberpunk.rule.aimed-shots.cost_or_limit: Uses the whole Action and is limited to one rate of fire.
cyberpunk.rule.aimed-shots.who_may: Attackers making ranged or melee attacks
cyberpunk.rule.aimed-shots.blocked_reason: This is a game procedure, not a world mechanism.

cyberpunk.rule.autofire.name: Autofire

effect.summary: An Autofire attack spends an Action and ten bullets, uses Autofire skill, and scales 2d6 damage by the amount the attack beats its DV.

cyberpunk.rule.autofire.cost_or_limit: Requires ten bullets; damage multiplier is capped by the weapon's Autofire rating; cannot make an Aimed Shot.
cyberpunk.rule.autofire.go_wrong: A double six on damage also causes a Critical Injury.
cyberpunk.rule.autofire.combines: Targets with REF 8 or higher may attempt to dodge.
cyberpunk.rule.autofire.mechanism: Ammunition expenditure and variable attack damage
cyberpunk.rule.autofire.blocked_reason: The effect follows the passage's ordinary attack and damage procedures.

cyberpunk.rule.arrows.name: Arrows

effect.summary: Loading an arrow is part of a bow or crossbow attack, so those weapons do not use the Reload Action.

cyberpunk.rule.arrows.cost_or_limit: Basic arrows can be retrieved after firing.
cyberpunk.rule.arrows.blocked_reason: This is a game procedure, not a world mechanism.

cyberpunk.rule.suppressive-fire.name: Suppressive Fire

effect.summary: Spending an Action and ten bullets can force exposed people in sight within 25 metres/yards to seek cover if they fail a contest.

cyberpunk.rule.suppressive-fire.cost_or_limit: Targets who cannot reach cover with their next Move Action must also Run toward it.
cyberpunk.rule.suppressive-fire.combines: Uses a WILL and Concentration contest against the attacker's REF and Autofire.
cyberpunk.rule.suppressive-fire.blocked_reason: The rule affects multiple targets within a defined area.

cyberpunk.rule.shotgun-shells.name: Shotgun Shells

effect.summary: A successful DV13 attack deals one shared 3d6 damage roll to visible targets within six metres/yards in front of the shooter.

cyberpunk.rule.shotgun-shells.cost_or_limit: Cannot be used for an Aimed Shot; each target with REF 8 or higher may dodge.
cyberpunk.rule.shotgun-shells.blocked_reason: It affects several targets in a defined area in front of the shooter.

cyberpunk.rule.explosives.name: Explosives

effect.summary: Explosive weapons damage all targets and terrain in a 10-by-10-metre/yard area centered on the intended target.

cyberpunk.rule.explosives.cost_or_limit: A missed attack lands at the GM's chosen point within that area; qualifying targets can dodge outside the blast.
cyberpunk.rule.explosives.go_wrong: A blast cannot harm someone behind cover that the blast cannot destroy.
cyberpunk.rule.explosives.combines: The damage roll is shared among targets.
cyberpunk.rule.explosives.blocked_reason: The rule applies damage to a spatial area and permits individual escape from it.

cyberpunk.rule.melee-armor-penetration.name: Melee armor penetration

effect.summary: Melee weapon attacks and Martial Arts attacks ignore half of the defender's armor, rounded up.

cyberpunk.rule.melee-armor-penetration.cost_or_limit: Brawling attacks do not ignore half the defender's armor.
cyberpunk.rule.melee-armor-penetration.who_may: Melee weapon and Martial Arts attackers
cyberpunk.rule.melee-armor-penetration.blocked_reason: This is a combat damage rule.

cyberpunk.rule.grappling.name: Grappling

effect.summary: A successful Grab can hold a target or take an object; a grapple restricts movement and imposes -2 to Actions.

cyberpunk.rule.grappling.cost_or_limit: Initiating a Grab requires a free hand; grappled characters cannot use two-handed weapons.
cyberpunk.rule.grappling.who_may: Characters in reach who can make a Grab
cyberpunk.rule.grappling.combines: Choking and throwing require a grappled target.
cyberpunk.rule.grappling.blocked_reason: This is a game procedure, not a world mechanism.

cyberpunk.rule.choke.name: Choke

effect.summary: A grappling attacker deals BODY damage directly to the target's HP, ignoring armor.

cyberpunk.rule.choke.cost_or_limit: Requires being the attacker in a grapple; three successive rounds of choking make the target unconscious.
cyberpunk.rule.choke.go_wrong: If it would reduce a target above 1 HP below zero, the target instead remains at 1 HP and becomes unconscious.
cyberpunk.rule.choke.mind: Causes unconsciousness in the stated cases.
cyberpunk.rule.choke.combines: Requires a Grab; damage does not ablate armor.
cyberpunk.rule.choke.blocked_reason: The described damage and unconsciousness use the basic effect grammar.

cyberpunk.rule.choking-and-asphyxiation.name: Choking and asphyxiation

effect.summary: After holding breath for BODY minutes, drowning deals BODY damage directly to HP at the start of each turn; asphyxiation follows the same rule.

cyberpunk.rule.choking-and-asphyxiation.cost_or_limit: Space exposure also deals 1d6 damage each turn to INT, REF, and DEX; INT reaching zero means death, and these stat losses reverse after breathing air.
cyberpunk.rule.choking-and-asphyxiation.combines: Drowning damage ignores armor and does not ablate it.
cyberpunk.rule.choking-and-asphyxiation.mechanism: Breath capacity, vitality loss, and stat damage
cyberpunk.rule.choking-and-asphyxiation.blocked_reason: These are direct damage and recovery rules.

cyberpunk.rule.electrocution.name: Electrocution

effect.summary: Electrocution immediately deals 6d6 damage, repeating at the end of each turn while the victim remains in contact.

cyberpunk.rule.electrocution.cost_or_limit: Armor absorbs damage normally; repeated damage starts at the end of the next turn.
cyberpunk.rule.electrocution.blocked_reason: The hazard uses ordinary damage and turn timing.

cyberpunk.rule.exposure.name: Exposure

effect.summary: Extreme environmental exposure deals 1d6 direct HP damage at each day's end.

cyberpunk.rule.exposure.cost_or_limit: While exposed, natural healing is impossible even if stabilized; proper environmental equipment prevents exposure risk.
cyberpunk.rule.exposure.mechanism: Ongoing environmental harm and healing restriction
cyberpunk.rule.exposure.blocked_reason: The damage and healing restriction can be represented.

cyberpunk.rule.falling.name: Falling

effect.summary: Falls of at least ten metres/yards deal 2d6 damage per ten metres/yards fallen and may cause a Broken Leg.

cyberpunk.rule.falling.cost_or_limit: A nearby ledge allows one DV15 Athletics save; two Cyberlegs prevent harm only up to 30 metres/yards.
cyberpunk.rule.falling.go_wrong: Falling from a skyscraper without a parachute is stated to be fatal.
cyberpunk.rule.falling.blocked_reason: The effect is damage and injury based on fall distance.

cyberpunk.rule.poisons-and-drugs.name: Poisons and drugs

effect.summary: A failed Resist Torture/Drugs check against the attack DV applies the poison or drug's effect.

cyberpunk.rule.poisons-and-drugs.cost_or_limit: Armor is not ablated; listed poison intensities deal 1d6, 2d6, or 3d6 direct HP damage, while drugs may cause inebriation, suggestibility, or a design-specific effect.
cyberpunk.rule.poisons-and-drugs.mind: Some drug effects include suggestibility or inebriation.
cyberpunk.rule.poisons-and-drugs.who_may: Targets exposed to a poison or drug
cyberpunk.rule.poisons-and-drugs.combines: Effect depends on the substance and its DV.
cyberpunk.rule.poisons-and-drugs.blocked_reason: Suggestibility changes a character's mind and behavior.

cyberpunk.rule.radiation.name: Radiation

effect.summary: High radiation causes mild-fire-level damage each turn in a hot zone, or deadly-fire-level damage in an extremely hot zone.

cyberpunk.rule.radiation.cost_or_limit: Low-level exposure causes gradual sickness and eventual death; occupants cannot use an Action to extinguish high-radiation damage while in the zone.
cyberpunk.rule.radiation.combines: Environmental damage cannot cause Critical Injuries.
cyberpunk.rule.radiation.mechanism: Persistent area hazard and long-term radiation harm
cyberpunk.rule.radiation.blocked_reason: The hazard applies to anyone remaining within a defined hot zone.

cyberpunk.rule.cover-requires-concealmen.name: Cover requires concealment from line of sight

effect.summary: A character is in cover only when fully behind something that can stop a bullet and enemies lack line of sight.

cyberpunk.rule.cover-requires-concealmen.cost_or_limit: There is no partial cover; ineffective material provides no cover or HP.
cyberpunk.rule.cover-requires-concealmen.go_wrong: An enemy can move to regain line of sight.
cyberpunk.rule.cover-requires-concealmen.combines: Cover can be removed by destroying it.
cyberpunk.rule.cover-requires-concealmen.blocked_reason: A binary cover condition can be represented as a rule.

cyberpunk.rule.cover-durability-and-dest.name: Cover durability and destruction

effect.summary: Cover has HP by material and thickness; at zero HP it is destroyed, and excess damage is lost.

cyberpunk.rule.cover-durability-and-dest.cost_or_limit: A 2 m by 2 m section is attacked separately; explosives are an exception.
cyberpunk.rule.cover-durability-and-dest.go_wrong: Damage in excess of cover HP does not harm those hiding behind it.
cyberpunk.rule.cover-durability-and-dest.combines: Material and thickness set HP; thin cover may shift, while thick cover needs BODY 10 or special equipment to move.
cyberpunk.rule.cover-durability-and-dest.mechanism: Hit-point durability and material-based damage thresholds.
cyberpunk.rule.cover-durability-and-dest.blocked_reason: The many material-specific HP values require material rows or a material lookup beyond the basic effect grammar.

cyberpunk.rule.steel-cover-resists-unarm.name: Steel cover resists unarmed attacks

effect.summary: Martial Arts and Brawling cannot damage steel cover unless the attacker has a Cyberarm or BODY 10 or higher.

cyberpunk.rule.steel-cover-resists-unarm.combines: Attacker needs a Cyberarm or BODY 10+ to overcome the restriction.
cyberpunk.rule.steel-cover-resists-unarm.blocked_reason: A conditional restriction is directly representable as a rule.

cyberpunk.rule.using-a-shield-occupies-a.name: Using a shield occupies a hand

effect.summary: Equipping or dropping a shield takes an Action, and the carrying hand cannot do other things.

cyberpunk.rule.using-a-shield-occupies-a.cost_or_limit: A shield with HP remaining makes its wielder count as in cover.
cyberpunk.rule.using-a-shield-occupies-a.go_wrong: A shield at zero HP is destroyed and no longer gives cover, though it remains in hand until dropped.
cyberpunk.rule.using-a-shield-occupies-a.combines: When interposed against a visible attacker, the wielder cannot dodge that attack.
cyberpunk.rule.using-a-shield-occupies-a.mechanism: Action cost, occupied hand, and shield hit-point state.
cyberpunk.rule.using-a-shield-occupies-a.blocked_reason: The hand-use and shield-state constraints can be represented as rules.

cyberpunk.rule.human-shield-restrictions.name: Human shield restrictions

effect.summary: A grappled defender can be wielded as cover, but not against melee attacks or aimed shots at the wielder's head.

cyberpunk.rule.human-shield-restrictions.cost_or_limit: The wielder cannot use the shielded person to dodge ranged attacks; a live shield is unequipped by ending the Grapple.
cyberpunk.rule.human-shield-restrictions.go_wrong: If the person dies while equipped, they become a corpse shield with HP equal to BODY.
cyberpunk.rule.human-shield-restrictions.mind: The living shield may squirm, making it unwieldy.
cyberpunk.rule.human-shield-restrictions.who_may: A character who is the Attacker in a Grapple and has no other shield equipped.
cyberpunk.rule.human-shield-restrictions.combines: The wielder may attack the shield; dropping a corpse shield costs an Action.
cyberpunk.rule.human-shield-restrictions.mechanism: Grapple-based cover and death-triggered state change.
cyberpunk.rule.human-shield-restrictions.blocked_reason: The restrictions and death-triggered shield state can be represented as rules.

cyberpunk.rule.armor-protection-and-pena.name: Armor protection and penalties

effect.summary: Only the highest worn SP at each location applies, while all worn armor there ablates together.

cyberpunk.rule.armor-protection-and-pena.cost_or_limit: The most severe armor penalty applies once and can reduce MOVE to zero.
cyberpunk.rule.armor-protection-and-pena.go_wrong: Armor loses 1 SP on a location when damage gets through.
cyberpunk.rule.armor-protection-and-pena.combines: Armor may be worn on head or body; some damage types bypass armor.
cyberpunk.rule.armor-protection-and-pena.mechanism: Location-based damage reduction, degradation, and movement penalties.
cyberpunk.rule.armor-protection-and-pena.blocked_reason: The protection, stacking restriction, and degradation can be implemented as rules.

cyberpunk.rule.death-saves.name: Death Saves

effect.summary: A mortally wounded character rolls a d10 at the start of each Turn; a roll below BODY survives and a 10 fails automatically.

cyberpunk.rule.death-saves.cost_or_limit: Each roll adds +1 to future Death Save difficulty; stabilization at 1 HP resets the penalty to its base value.
cyberpunk.rule.death-saves.go_wrong: One failed Death Save means death.
cyberpunk.rule.death-saves.combines: Critical Injuries can increase the base Death Save penalty.
cyberpunk.rule.death-saves.mechanism: Escalating repeated survival check with irreversible death on failure.
cyberpunk.rule.death-saves.blocked_reason: A timed check with a cumulative modifier and failure state is directly expressible as a rule.

cyberpunk.rule.critical-injury-bonus-dam.name: Critical Injury bonus damage

effect.summary: Two or more damage dice showing six cause a Critical Injury, which adds 5 damage directly to Hit Points.

cyberpunk.rule.critical-injury-bonus-dam.cost_or_limit: The bonus damage ignores armor and hit location; injury tables determine additional effects.
cyberpunk.rule.critical-injury-bonus-dam.go_wrong: Mortally wounded characters also suffer a Critical Injury whenever an attack damages them.
cyberpunk.rule.critical-injury-bonus-dam.mind: Some injuries impair actions, movement, senses, or speech.
cyberpunk.rule.critical-injury-bonus-dam.who_may: Targets of melee or ranged attacks.
cyberpunk.rule.critical-injury-bonus-dam.combines: Aimed headshots use the head injury table; other attacks use the body table.
cyberpunk.rule.critical-injury-bonus-dam.mechanism: Damage-triggered injury state and direct HP loss.
cyberpunk.rule.critical-injury-bonus-dam.blocked_reason: The passage specifies many persistent injury effects and conditional changes that exceed a single basic damage effect.

cyberpunk.rule.vehicle-structural-damage.name: Vehicle Structural Damage Points

effect.summary: Vehicles with at least 1 SDP can move; at zero they are destroyed, cease to be cover, and cannot move until repaired.

cyberpunk.rule.vehicle-structural-damage.cost_or_limit: Repair requires the appropriate Vehicle Tech Skill.
cyberpunk.rule.vehicle-structural-damage.combines: Vehicle glass has no HP and gives no cover.
cyberpunk.rule.vehicle-structural-damage.mechanism: Vehicle durability threshold and repair state.
cyberpunk.rule.vehicle-structural-damage.blocked_reason: A durability threshold and repair requirement are directly representable as rules.

cyberpunk.rule.vehicle-movement-and-driv.name: Vehicle movement and driver control

effect.summary: Starting a vehicle places its driver first in Initiative and uses the driver's MOVE as the vehicle's MOVE.

cyberpunk.rule.vehicle-movement-and-driv.cost_or_limit: Starting and stopping take an Action; without Interface Plugs a driving hand is required, and letting go causes loss of control next Turn.
cyberpunk.rule.vehicle-movement-and-driv.go_wrong: Failed driving checks or maneuvers cause loss of control; the GM decides movement for that Turn.
cyberpunk.rule.vehicle-movement-and-driv.combines: Interface Plugs permit hands-free driving; a driver cannot use the Run Action while the vehicle is started.
cyberpunk.rule.vehicle-movement-and-driv.mechanism: Vehicle operation tied to driver actions, checks, and movement.
cyberpunk.rule.vehicle-movement-and-driv.blocked_reason: The action, check, and vehicle-state requirements can be represented as rules.

cyberpunk.rule.ramming.name: Ramming

effect.summary: A vehicle that hits a person, cover, or vehicle deals 6d6 damage to both, and crash participants suffer Whiplash.

cyberpunk.rule.ramming.cost_or_limit: Movement continues through destroyed cover or vehicles, but otherwise stops; pedestrians can remain atop the vehicle after impact.
cyberpunk.rule.ramming.go_wrong: A pedestrian who survives may choose to be on top of the vehicle.
cyberpunk.rule.ramming.combines: A person on foot can dodge a ramming vehicle with a DV13 check.
cyberpunk.rule.ramming.mechanism: Collision damage, movement interruption, and injury consequence.
cyberpunk.rule.ramming.blocked_reason: The collision rule includes damage, injury, and conditional movement outcomes.

cyberpunk.rule.reputation.name: Reputation

effect.summary: A character's deeds establish a public reputation that affects whether new people have heard of them.

cyberpunk.rule.reputation.cost_or_limit: A higher-level deed replaces a lower-level reputation; most characters start at zero.
cyberpunk.rule.reputation.go_wrong: Negative deeds can replace positive reputation and turn recognition against the character.
cyberpunk.rule.reputation.mind: A listener who recognizes the character may react favorably or unfavorably.
cyberpunk.rule.reputation.who_may: Characters whose actions earn a reputation, as awarded by the GM.
cyberpunk.rule.reputation.combines: Recognition is tested when meeting new people; Reputation also contributes to Facedowns.
cyberpunk.rule.reputation.mechanism: Public notoriety with graded recognition and social consequences.
cyberpunk.rule.reputation.blocked_reason: A graded social reputation state and its check can be implemented as a rule.

cyberpunk.rule.facedowns.name: Facedowns

effect.summary: Participants compare COOL, Reputation, and a die; the loser backs down or suffers a penalty against the winner.

cyberpunk.rule.facedowns.cost_or_limit: A tie has no effect; cowardice makes the defining Reputation negative.
cyberpunk.rule.facedowns.go_wrong: The loser who refuses to back down takes -2 to future Actions against the winner until defeating them once.
cyberpunk.rule.facedowns.who_may: Participants in a confrontation when the GM calls for it.
cyberpunk.rule.facedowns.combines: Uses the participants' Reputation, which may be negative for cowardice.
cyberpunk.rule.facedowns.mechanism: Opposed social check with a fear penalty or withdrawal outcome.
cyberpunk.rule.facedowns.blocked_reason: The opposed check and its temporary penalty can be represented as a rule.

cyberpunk.rule.net-access-and-jacking-ou.name: NET access and Jacking Out

effect.summary: Netrunning requires Interface; Jacking In requires being within 6 m of an access point, generally without a wall in between.

cyberpunk.rule.net-access-and-jacking-ou.cost_or_limit: Moving out of range automatically jacks the user out; a safe Jack Out resets Architecture defenses and forces a restart from the original access point.
cyberpunk.rule.net-access-and-jacking-ou.go_wrong: An involuntary exit triggers remaining encountered enemy Black ICE effects.
cyberpunk.rule.net-access-and-jacking-ou.mind: Without Virtuality Goggles, the user is effectively unconscious in Meatspace until Jacking Out.
cyberpunk.rule.net-access-and-jacking-ou.combines: Programs leave with the Netrunner; a lasting Architecture change requires reaching the bottom and leaving a Virus.
cyberpunk.rule.net-access-and-jacking-ou.mechanism: Range-gated network access with safe and unsafe exit states.
cyberpunk.rule.net-access-and-jacking-ou.blocked_reason: The access, range, and exit conditions are directly expressible as rules.

cyberpunk.rule.net-action-limit.name: NET Action limit

effect.summary: On a Turn, a Netrunner chooses a Meat Action or a number of NET Actions set by Interface Rank, and still gets a Move Action.

cyberpunk.rule.net-action-limit.cost_or_limit: Interface ranks 1–3 allow 2 NET Actions, ranks 4–6 allow 3, ranks 7–9 allow 4, and rank 10 allows 5.
cyberpunk.rule.net-action-limit.go_wrong: Without the Interface Role Ability, a character cannot Netrun.
cyberpunk.rule.net-action-limit.combines: Moving and saving copies of Files do not use NET Actions.
cyberpunk.rule.net-action-limit.blocked_reason: The rank-based action limit is a straightforward procedure.

cyberpunk.rule.net-movement-and-file-cop.name: NET movement and File copies

effect.summary: Movement within an Architecture and saving a File copy do not use NET Actions.

cyberpunk.rule.net-movement-and-file-cop.cost_or_limit: Movement cannot pass an obstruction such as a Password.
cyberpunk.rule.net-movement-and-file-cop.go_wrong: Pushing past an obstruction can be fatal.
cyberpunk.rule.net-movement-and-file-cop.combines: Other actions in an Architecture generally require NET Actions.
cyberpunk.rule.net-movement-and-file-cop.mechanism: Action-exempt movement and data copying, constrained by obstructions.
cyberpunk.rule.net-movement-and-file-cop.blocked_reason: The action exemptions and movement limit are directly expressible as rules.

cyberpunk.rule.net-control-node-contests.name: NET control-node contests

effect.summary: A Control Node can be activated once per Turn; wresting one from another controller requires beating their control check.

cyberpunk.rule.net-control-node-contests.cost_or_limit: Operating each attached device requires a separate NET Action; control ends on Jack Out.
cyberpunk.rule.net-control-node-contests.go_wrong: A rival Netrunner or Demon can take control by beating the current controller's check.
cyberpunk.rule.net-control-node-contests.who_may: Netrunners and Demons contending for Nodes.
cyberpunk.rule.net-control-node-contests.combines: Control of the Node permits operation of connected devices from anywhere in the Architecture.
cyberpunk.rule.net-control-node-contests.mechanism: Exclusive, contested control of network devices.
cyberpunk.rule.net-control-node-contests.blocked_reason: The rule explicitly models competing powers contesting an already-held control state.

cyberpunk.rule.cyberdeck-option-slots.name: Cyberdeck Option Slots

effect.summary: Hardware uses one Option Slot unless an entry specifies otherwise.

cyberpunk.rule.cyberdeck-option-slots.cost_or_limit: Deck capacity is limited; the user must allocate slots among Programs and Hardware.
cyberpunk.rule.cyberdeck-option-slots.combines: Programs and Black ICE also use Cyberdeck slots.
cyberpunk.rule.cyberdeck-option-slots.blocked_reason: A finite equipment slot limit is directly representable.

cyberpunk.rule.program-derezz-and-recove.name: Program Derezz and recovery

effect.summary: At zero REZ a Program is useless but remains present; recovery costs two NET Actions, while destruction erases it permanently.

cyberpunk.rule.program-derezz-and-recove.combines: Attack Programs automatically deactivate after use.
cyberpunk.rule.program-derezz-and-recove.blocked_reason: The distinction between depleted, restored, and permanently erased states needs item-state tracking.

cyberpunk.rule.program-activation-limit.name: Program activation limit

effect.summary: Each Cyberdeck Program can be activated once per Meatspace Round, and a Rezzed Program cannot be activated again until deactivated.

cyberpunk.rule.program-activation-limit.cost_or_limit: Multiple copies may bypass the limit; simultaneous effects stack unless noted.
cyberpunk.rule.program-activation-limit.combines: Attack Programs deactivate themselves after use.
cyberpunk.rule.program-activation-limit.blocked_reason: A per-round usage limit can be implemented as a rule.

cyberpunk.rule.program-installation-time.name: Program installation time

effect.summary: Installing or uninstalling a Program takes an hour.

cyberpunk.rule.program-installation-time.cost_or_limit: One hour per installation or removal.
cyberpunk.rule.program-installation-time.combines: Black ICE installation and removal also takes an hour.
cyberpunk.rule.program-installation-time.blocked_reason: A time cost can be applied directly.

cyberpunk.rule.black-ice-pursuit-and-sli.name: Black ICE pursuit and Slide

effect.summary: Black ICE pursues its target through an Architecture until Derezzed or successfully eluded with Slide; then it waits at the point of escape.

cyberpunk.rule.black-ice-pursuit-and-sli.cost_or_limit: Demon Black ICE cannot be eluded with Slide.
cyberpunk.rule.black-ice-pursuit-and-sli.go_wrong: A failed Slide does not stop pursuit.
cyberpunk.rule.black-ice-pursuit-and-sli.mind: Black ICE follows its single coded purpose.
cyberpunk.rule.black-ice-pursuit-and-sli.who_may: Applies to Black ICE and Netrunners.
cyberpunk.rule.black-ice-pursuit-and-sli.combines: Slide changes the ICE's pursuit state.
cyberpunk.rule.black-ice-pursuit-and-sli.blocked_reason: The rule requires tracking a Program's pursuit and waiting states.

cyberpunk.rule.black-ice-targeting-limit.name: Black ICE targeting limit

effect.summary: Black ICE can do only what it was coded to do and cannot act as a digital pet.

cyberpunk.rule.black-ice-targeting-limit.cost_or_limit: Its behavior is restricted to its one coded task.
cyberpunk.rule.black-ice-targeting-limit.blocked_reason: A fixed behavior restriction is directly implementable.

cyberpunk.rule.demon-awareness-and-initi.name: Demon awareness and initiative

effect.summary: A Demon knows its Architecture, ignores Passwords, detects Netrunners, and automatically wins Speed contests against Programs.

cyberpunk.rule.demon-awareness-and-initi.cost_or_limit: Demons have no SPD or PER and cannot be Slid away from.
cyberpunk.rule.demon-awareness-and-initi.mind: Intelligence is limited to predetermined triggers.
cyberpunk.rule.demon-awareness-and-initi.combines: Detection can place a Demon at the top of the Initiative Queue.
cyberpunk.rule.demon-awareness-and-initi.blocked_reason: These are discrete awareness and contest rules.

cyberpunk.rule.cyberware-and-architectur.name: Cyberware and Architecture access

effect.summary: Cyberware cannot be hacked using Interface because it does not operate through a NET Architecture; Cybertech governs it.

cyberpunk.rule.cyberware-and-architectur.who_may: Applies to Netrunners and users of Cyberware.
cyberpunk.rule.cyberware-and-architectur.combines: Analog devices and some CitiNet-connected electronics also lack an Architecture.
cyberpunk.rule.cyberware-and-architectur.blocked_reason: The rule specifies which skill applies to a target.

cyberpunk.rule.net-architecture-branchin.name: NET Architecture branching and floor count

effect.summary: Architecture shape uses 3d6 floors; branches may begin only after the second main-branch floor, and a longest branch defines the bottom.

cyberpunk.rule.net-architecture-branchin.cost_or_limit: Branches are randomly added on a d10 result of seven or higher, repeating until a lower result.
cyberpunk.rule.net-architecture-branchin.combines: The bottom permits a Netrunner to leave a Virus.
cyberpunk.rule.net-architecture-branchin.blocked_reason: The rule describes a structural generation procedure.

cyberpunk.rule.net-architecture-purchase.name: NET Architecture purchase limits

effect.summary: Purchased Architecture length sets portability and maximum Control Nodes, and its floor count cannot be increased later.

cyberpunk.rule.net-architecture-purchase.cost_or_limit: Three-to-six floors allow two nodes and portability; seven-to-twelve allow three nodes; thirteen-to-eighteen have no stated node capacity and are not portable.
cyberpunk.rule.net-architecture-purchase.go_wrong: The floor count cannot be expanded after purchase.
cyberpunk.rule.net-architecture-purchase.who_may: Buyers at a qualifying Night Market.
cyberpunk.rule.net-architecture-purchase.combines: Purchase requires a Night Market with Personal Electronics and a Fixer of Rank 4 or higher.
cyberpunk.rule.net-architecture-purchase.blocked_reason: Fixed capacity and purchase limits are directly representable.

cyberpunk.rule.net-architecture-program-.name: NET Architecture program costs and placement

effect.summary: none

cyberpunk.rule.net-architecture-program-.cost_or_limit: Each program is paid for separately; multiple Black ICE on one floor multiply the cost by their number, but Demons cannot be doubled or tripled.
cyberpunk.rule.net-architecture-program-.combines: Black ICE prices match those for Cyberdecks.
cyberpunk.rule.net-architecture-program-.blocked_reason: This is a purchase and placement restriction, not an unrepresented effect.

cyberpunk.rule.net-architecture-demon-li.name: NET Architecture Demon limit

effect.summary: none

cyberpunk.rule.net-architecture-demon-li.cost_or_limit: At most one Demon per six floors; Demons cannot be placed in multiples on one floor.
cyberpunk.rule.net-architecture-demon-li.blocked_reason: A numeric capacity limit can be enforced directly.

cyberpunk.rule.net-architecture-program-.name: NET Architecture program availability

effect.summary: none

cyberpunk.rule.net-architecture-program-.cost_or_limit: NET Architecture programs are sold only at Night Markets with Personal Electronics run by a Rank 4 or higher Fixer.
cyberpunk.rule.net-architecture-program-.who_may: Purchasers meeting the market access condition.
cyberpunk.rule.net-architecture-program-.blocked_reason: This is a straightforward access restriction.

cyberpunk.rule.defense-pricing-and-avail.name: Defense pricing and availability

effect.summary: none

cyberpunk.rule.defense-pricing-and-avail.cost_or_limit: Defense cost follows counter DV: DV9 is 500eb, DV13 is 1,000eb, DV17 is 5,000eb, and DV21 is 10,000eb.
cyberpunk.rule.defense-pricing-and-avail.who_may: Purchasers at a qualifying Night Market.
cyberpunk.rule.defense-pricing-and-avail.where_from: Night Market with Personal Electronics, run by a Rank 4 or higher Fixer.
cyberpunk.rule.defense-pricing-and-avail.combines: Defenses need a way to distinguish friends from foes.
cyberpunk.rule.defense-pricing-and-avail.blocked_reason: The rule is a cost schedule and availability restriction.

cyberpunk.rule.critical-injury-triggers-.name: Critical Injury triggers and bonus damage

effect.summary: none

cyberpunk.rule.critical-injury-triggers-.cost_or_limit: Two or more damage dice showing 6 on a melee or ranged attack cause a Critical Injury; each causes 5 bonus HP damage that ignores armor and hit location.
cyberpunk.rule.critical-injury-triggers-.go_wrong: A Mortally Wounded character suffers a Critical Injury whenever damaged by an attack.
cyberpunk.rule.critical-injury-triggers-.combines: Injury results are rolled on the appropriate table, avoiding injuries the target already has.
cyberpunk.rule.critical-injury-triggers-.mechanism: Damage-triggered injury and fixed bonus damage.
cyberpunk.rule.critical-injury-triggers-.blocked_reason: The rule is a combat trigger and direct vitality loss.

cyberpunk.rule.stabilization.name: Stabilization

effect.summary: none

cyberpunk.rule.stabilization.cost_or_limit: An Action and TECH plus First Aid or Paramedic; DV10, 13, or 15 for Lightly, Seriously, or Mortally Wounded targets.
cyberpunk.rule.stabilization.go_wrong: A patient who pushes beyond light activity during recovery loses that day's healing and must be stabilized again.
cyberpunk.rule.stabilization.who_may: A character treating themself or another target.
cyberpunk.rule.stabilization.combines: Mortally Wounded targets stabilize directly to 1 HP and become unconscious for one minute.
cyberpunk.rule.stabilization.blocked_reason: The rule uses a skill check and vitality recovery.

cyberpunk.rule.natural-healing-after-sta.name: Natural healing after stabilization

effect.summary: A stabilized character resting with light activity regains HP equal to BODY per full day until fully healed.

cyberpunk.rule.natural-healing-after-sta.cost_or_limit: Requires spending the majority of each day resting; pushing oneself prevents healing and reopens wounds.
cyberpunk.rule.natural-healing-after-sta.go_wrong: Overexertion restarts the need for stabilization.
cyberpunk.rule.natural-healing-after-sta.combines: Mortally Wounded characters instead receive 1 HP and unconsciousness on successful stabilization.
cyberpunk.rule.natural-healing-after-sta.mechanism: Daily vitality regeneration gated by rest.
cyberpunk.rule.natural-healing-after-sta.blocked_reason: The rule is ordinary vitality recovery with a rest condition.

cyberpunk.rule.quick-fix-and-treatment.name: Quick Fix and Treatment

effect.summary: A Quick Fix suppresses an injury effect for the day; Treatment removes it permanently.

cyberpunk.rule.quick-fix-and-treatment.cost_or_limit: Each Quick Fix takes one minute; Treatment takes four hours. A character cannot treat themself, but can Quick Fix themself.
cyberpunk.rule.quick-fix-and-treatment.who_may: A character with the required skill.
cyberpunk.rule.quick-fix-and-treatment.combines: The usable skill depends on injury severity; Cybertech may substitute for cyberware-related injuries.
cyberpunk.rule.quick-fix-and-treatment.blocked_reason: The effects are condition removal over stated durations.

cyberpunk.rule.trauma-team-plans-and-cov.name: Trauma Team plans and coverage transfer

effect.summary: none

cyberpunk.rule.trauma-team-plans-and-cov.cost_or_limit: Silver costs 500eb per month and charges hospital-equivalent fees for Surgery treatments; Executive costs 1,000eb monthly and includes those treatments. Either plan can cover one friend instead of its holder, but not two people at once.
cyberpunk.rule.trauma-team-plans-and-cov.go_wrong: Repeated calls for trivial injuries may lead to a missed future response.
cyberpunk.rule.trauma-team-plans-and-cov.who_may: Trauma Team plan members and, within the transfer limit, one friend.
cyberpunk.rule.trauma-team-plans-and-cov.combines: A registered card and linked Biomonitor can call automatically under the described injury conditions.
cyberpunk.rule.trauma-team-plans-and-cov.mechanism: Subscription service and one-to-one coverage limit.
cyberpunk.rule.trauma-team-plans-and-cov.blocked_reason: This rule is a service access and usage limit.

cyberpunk.rule.trauma-team-call-and-arri.name: Trauma Team call and arrival

effect.summary: A call brings the team after a random delay of one to six rounds, entering at the top of Initiative.

cyberpunk.rule.trauma-team-call-and-arri.cost_or_limit: Calling is an Action unless the registered Agent and linked Biomonitor trigger an automatic call under the stated conditions; covered plans cannot serve multiple friends simultaneously.
cyberpunk.rule.trauma-team-call-and-arri.go_wrong: The team may fail to respond after repeated frivolous calls.
cyberpunk.rule.trauma-team-call-and-arri.who_may: Injured callers and eligible registered Biomonitor users.
cyberpunk.rule.trauma-team-call-and-arri.combines: The team's members use combat numbers for attacks, defense, and listed skills; they cannot dodge bullets.
cyberpunk.rule.trauma-team-call-and-arri.blocked_reason: The response is a delayed movement and initiative entry.

cyberpunk.rule.cyberware-harvesting-from.name: Cyberware harvesting from corpses

effect.summary: A Medtech can harvest most cyberware from a corpse without destroying it by succeeding at the installation DV.

cyberpunk.rule.cyberware-harvesting-from.cost_or_limit: Takes four hours; failure destroys the cyberware and wastes two hours. Easily removable items are exceptions; forceful removal takes a minute but leaves it needing repair.
cyberpunk.rule.cyberware-harvesting-from.who_may: A Medtech, except for items easily removed with an Action.
cyberpunk.rule.cyberware-harvesting-from.blocked_reason: The rule is an item removal and damage procedure.

cyberpunk.rule.cyberware-installation.name: Cyberware installation

effect.summary: Installing cyberware in another person requires surgery and causes the patient Humanity Loss as normal.

cyberpunk.rule.cyberware-installation.cost_or_limit: Hospital DVs and costs are Mall DV13/100eb, Clinic DV15/500eb, and Hospital DV17/1,000eb; installation surgery cannot be done on oneself unless typical installation is Mall.
cyberpunk.rule.cyberware-installation.go_wrong: Failed harvesting destroys cyberware; failed procedures waste operating time as described.
cyberpunk.rule.cyberware-installation.who_may: A Medtech performs surgery; self-installation is generally barred.
cyberpunk.rule.cyberware-installation.combines: Installation cost is generally included when purchasing cyberware.
cyberpunk.rule.cyberware-installation.mechanism: Surgery-gated item installation with personal cost.
cyberpunk.rule.cyberware-installation.blocked_reason: Cyberware is installed into a body and may provide equipment effects or upgrades not represented by the basic grammar.

cyberpunk.rule.street-drug-addiction.name: Street drug addiction

effect.summary: none

cyberpunk.rule.street-drug-addiction.cost_or_limit: After a drug's primary effect ends, roll WILL plus Resist Torture/Drugs and a d10 against its secondary-effect DV; multiple doses extend the primary duration by a full duration each.
cyberpunk.rule.street-drug-addiction.go_wrong: Failing the roll produces a permanent, habit-forming secondary effect until therapy.
cyberpunk.rule.street-drug-addiction.mind: Addiction may impose cravings, hallucinations, or attribute and skill penalties as specified by the drug.
cyberpunk.rule.street-drug-addiction.who_may: Anyone dosed with a listed street drug.
cyberpunk.rule.street-drug-addiction.combines: A dose can be administered by Airhypo or a successful melee attack.
cyberpunk.rule.street-drug-addiction.mechanism: Timed drug effect followed by a resistance check and persistent condition.
cyberpunk.rule.street-drug-addiction.blocked_reason: Persistent addiction states and drug-specific mental side effects are not captured by the basic effect grammar.

cyberpunk.rule.therapy-addiction-relapse.name: Therapy addiction relapse limit

effect.summary: none

cyberpunk.rule.therapy-addiction-relapse.cost_or_limit: For one year after therapy frees a patient from an addiction, they automatically fail any roll against that drug's secondary effect.
cyberpunk.rule.therapy-addiction-relapse.go_wrong: Exposure to the drug's secondary-effect roll causes automatic relapse during the year.
cyberpunk.rule.therapy-addiction-relapse.mind: The rule imposes a relapse vulnerability.
cyberpunk.rule.therapy-addiction-relapse.combines: Applies to the former source drug's secondary effect.
cyberpunk.rule.therapy-addiction-relapse.blocked_reason: The rule creates a persistent mental vulnerability following treatment.

cyberpunk.rule.humanity-recovery-limits.name: Humanity recovery limits

effect.summary: none

cyberpunk.rule.humanity-recovery-limits.cost_or_limit: Standard therapy restores 2d6 Humanity and extreme therapy 4d6; each cyberware piece lowers maximum Humanity by 2, or 4 for borgware. Cyberware with zero installation Humanity Loss does not lower the maximum.
cyberpunk.rule.humanity-recovery-limits.go_wrong: Cyberware prevents full recovery until it is removed.
cyberpunk.rule.humanity-recovery-limits.mind: Humanity measures empathy and sense of self in this system.
cyberpunk.rule.humanity-recovery-limits.combines: Cyberware removal can raise the patient's recoverable maximum.
cyberpunk.rule.humanity-recovery-limits.mechanism: Bounded resource recovery with equipment-dependent cap.
cyberpunk.rule.humanity-recovery-limits.blocked_reason: The rule is a numerical recovery cap.

cyberpunk.rule.cyberware-and-cyberpsycho.name: Cyberware and cyberpsychosis

effect.summary: Voluntary excessive replacement or alteration of a functioning body can contribute to dissociation and cyberpsychosis; therapeutic replacement of a lost part does not.

cyberpunk.rule.cyberware-and-cyberpsycho.cost_or_limit: Humanity loss is associated with unnecessary or excessive augmentation; restoring a lost part with a cloned or medical-grade replacement does not increase dissociation.
cyberpunk.rule.cyberware-and-cyberpsycho.go_wrong: Dissociation and psychopathic tendencies can combine into cyberpsychosis.
cyberpunk.rule.cyberware-and-cyberpsycho.mind: Describes impaired empathy, self-regard, identity, and perception of others.
cyberpunk.rule.cyberware-and-cyberpsycho.who_may: Characters undergoing voluntary augmentation or severe trauma.
cyberpunk.rule.cyberware-and-cyberpsycho.combines: External and psychological trauma can also contribute.
cyberpunk.rule.cyberware-and-cyberpsycho.mechanism: Cumulative mental-state deterioration linked to augmentation and trauma.
cyberpunk.rule.cyberware-and-cyberpsycho.blocked_reason: The rule models persistent dissociation and personality change rather than a basic instantaneous mind effect.

cyberpunk.rule.humanity-loss-from-trauma.name: Humanity Loss from trauma

effect.summary: Traumatic events can cause Humanity Loss, with listed examples ranging from 1d6 to 2d6.

cyberpunk.rule.humanity-loss-from-trauma.cost_or_limit: Torture and witnessing horrific death or mutilation cause 1d6; long-term abuse, imprisonment, starvation, or prolonged danger can cause 2d6.
cyberpunk.rule.humanity-loss-from-trauma.go_wrong: Repeated trauma may contribute to cyberpsychosis.
cyberpunk.rule.humanity-loss-from-trauma.mind: Represents loss of empathy, self-regard, or sense of self.
cyberpunk.rule.humanity-loss-from-trauma.who_may: Characters who experience severe physical, mental, or environmental trauma.
cyberpunk.rule.humanity-loss-from-trauma.where_from: Trauma rules; the GM assigns losses for events.
cyberpunk.rule.humanity-loss-from-trauma.combines: Can compound with cyberware-related Humanity Loss.
cyberpunk.rule.humanity-loss-from-trauma.mechanism: Trauma-triggered reduction of a mental resource.
cyberpunk.rule.humanity-loss-from-trauma.blocked_reason: The stated effect is a direct numerical loss.

cyberpunk.rule.cyberpsychosis-thresholds.name: Cyberpsychosis thresholds

effect.summary: EMP 3 or more avoids the listed disorder; EMP 2 indicates borderline dissociation, EMP 1 borderline cyberpsychosis, and EMP 0 cyberpsychosis.

cyberpunk.rule.cyberpsychosis-thresholds.cost_or_limit: At EMP 0 with negative Humanity, the GM takes control until Humanity becomes positive again; the listed checklist trait counts increase with severity.
cyberpunk.rule.cyberpsychosis-thresholds.go_wrong: Low Empathy and negative Humanity can produce severe or extreme cyberpsychosis.
cyberpunk.rule.cyberpsychosis-thresholds.mind: The rule imposes dissociative and psychopathic roleplaying states.
cyberpunk.rule.cyberpsychosis-thresholds.who_may: Characters whose EMP falls to the listed thresholds.
cyberpunk.rule.cyberpsychosis-thresholds.combines: Voluntary unneeded cyberware and traumatic experiences can contribute.
cyberpunk.rule.cyberpsychosis-thresholds.mechanism: Attribute-threshold mental-state transition and control handoff.
cyberpunk.rule.cyberpsychosis-thresholds.blocked_reason: Persistent personality alteration and transferring control of a character to the GM are not represented by the basic effect grammar.

cyberpunk.rule.datakrash-prevalence.name: DataKrash prevalence

effect.summary: By 2022, the DataKrash virus infected 78.2% of the NET.

cyberpunk.rule.datakrash-prevalence.go_wrong: Most of the NET became compromised.
cyberpunk.rule.datakrash-prevalence.combines: Motivated creation of a secure uninfected database.

cyberpunk.rule.wasting-plague.name: Wasting Plague

effect.summary: Intestinal infection causes victims to starve despite eating.

cyberpunk.rule.wasting-plague.combines: A vaccine was eventually developed in Japan.

cyberpunk.rule.carbon-plague.name: Carbon Plague

effect.summary: Nanotech plague ravaged Night City for two weeks and primarily targeted adults.

cyberpunk.rule.carbon-plague.go_wrong: Caused deaths and left young people orphaned.
cyberpunk.rule.carbon-plague.where_from: Corporate AV crash near Night City.

effect.summary: Megacorporations operate nearly as nations, with their own laws, cities, factories, and armies.

cyberpunk.rule.corporate-employment-cont.name: Corporate employment contracts

effect.summary: Companies can require employees to stay for a specified term, with severe penalties for breaking the contract.

cyberpunk.rule.corporate-employment-cont.cost_or_limit: Terms range from a year to a lifetime; penalties can include wage garnishment, lawsuits, and loss of licenses.
cyberpunk.rule.corporate-employment-cont.go_wrong: Companies may use sabotage, software, booby traps, blackmail, kidnapping, or assassination to enforce loyalty.
cyberpunk.rule.corporate-employment-cont.combines: Extraction teams may try to remove contracted staff.

cyberpunk.rule.corporate-face-responsibi.name: Corporate Face responsibility

effect.summary: A corporation must designate its largest stockholder as a living Face who personally bears legal punishment for corporate wrongdoing.

cyberpunk.rule.corporate-face-responsibi.cost_or_limit: Required for legitimate incorporation in the named jurisdictions.
cyberpunk.rule.corporate-face-responsibi.go_wrong: The Face may face prison or death for corporate offenses.
cyberpunk.rule.corporate-face-responsibi.who_may: The corporation's largest stockholder is designated.
cyberpunk.rule.corporate-face-responsibi.where_from: Corporate-responsibility laws in the EuroTheatre, China, Free States, and New United States.
cyberpunk.rule.corporate-face-responsibi.combines: Replaces the older shield that insulated executives and boards.

cyberpunk.rule.ai-protocols.name: AI Protocols

effect.summary: Potentially restricts experiments involving cyberware gestalt and AI.

cyberpunk.rule.ai-protocols.cost_or_limit: The passage does not specify the protocols’ provisions.
cyberpunk.rule.ai-protocols.combines: Mentioned in connection with alleged cyberware gestalt research.
cyberpunk.rule.ai-protocols.blocked_reason: The rule is described as a possible legal violation, but its operative constraints are unspecified.

cyberpunk.rule.trauma-team-combat-rate.name: Trauma Team combat rate

effect.summary: Trauma Team charges combat rates if weapons are fired within half a kilometer.

cyberpunk.rule.trauma-team-combat-rate.cost_or_limit: The surcharge applies within a half-kilometer of gunfire.
cyberpunk.rule.trauma-team-combat-rate.where_from: Trauma Team policy during the war

cyberpunk.rule.garden-creator-revenue-sh.name: Garden creator revenue share

effect.summary: Creators receive ten percent of advertising revenue from Garden content.

cyberpunk.rule.garden-creator-revenue-sh.combines: Revenue is generated by targeted ads.

cyberpunk.rule.long-distance-citinet-com.name: Long-distance CitiNet communication

effect.summary: Intercity CitiNet communication sends text, voice, and video messages, not direct live audio or visual contact.

cyberpunk.rule.long-distance-citinet-com.cost_or_limit: Live direct contact requires a WorldSat contract.
cyberpunk.rule.long-distance-citinet-com.combines: Uses burst transfers over reclaimed lines, free-space optics, and Nomad couriers.

cyberpunk.rule.night-city-s-free-state-s.name: Night City's Free State status

effect.summary: Night City's independence left it outside the protection of a larger nation during the war.

cyberpunk.rule.night-city-s-free-state-s.go_wrong: It helped make the city a viable nuclear target.

cyberpunk.rule.air-blast-fallout.name: Air-blast fallout

effect.summary: A high-altitude blast reduced long-term radioactivity, while debris and fire still spread widely.

cyberpunk.rule.air-blast-fallout.cost_or_limit: Residual radioactivity remained, especially in surrounding towers.
cyberpunk.rule.air-blast-fallout.go_wrong: Particulate debris and firestorm affected broad regions.

cyberpunk.rule.liquefaction-of-night-cit.name: Liquefaction of Night City's fill

effect.summary: The blast and shaking destabilized fill and sand, causing parts of the city to liquefy and flood.

cyberpunk.rule.liquefaction-of-night-cit.cost_or_limit: Most severe in areas built on fill.
cyberpunk.rule.liquefaction-of-night-cit.go_wrong: Damaged foundations and infrastructure and flooded inner districts.

cyberpunk.rule.threat-rating-variation-w.name: Threat Rating variation within a region

effect.summary: A region's dominant Threat Rating does not prevent nearby areas from having different ratings or transitioning between ratings.

cyberpunk.rule.threat-rating-variation-w.cost_or_limit: A region may contain multiple ratings.

cyberpunk.rule.datakrash-network-restric.name: DataKrash network restriction

effect.summary: The DataKrash and destroyed infrastructure make the greater NET dangerous and inaccessible across much of its former extent.

cyberpunk.rule.datakrash-network-restric.cost_or_limit: Surviving traffic is limited to secured VPNs or isolated local systems.
cyberpunk.rule.datakrash-network-restric.go_wrong: Running the wider NET is nearly suicidal and may spread the Krash.
cyberpunk.rule.datakrash-network-restric.who_may: Netrunners face the restriction; Netwatch blocks access
cyberpunk.rule.datakrash-network-restric.where_from: Ihara-Grubb protocol systems and the global NET
cyberpunk.rule.datakrash-network-restric.combines: Netwatch destroys or disables key nodes

cyberpunk.rule.data-term-access-controls.name: Data Term access controls

effect.summary: Some public terminals can be rewired to require a pass card or payment before use.

cyberpunk.rule.data-term-access-controls.cost_or_limit: Access depends on the terminal's configured payment or credential requirement.

cyberpunk.rule.max-tac-prisoner-handling.name: MAX-TAC prisoner handling

effect.summary: MAX-TAC does not hold prisoners; it transfers arrestees to the local justice or security facility.

cyberpunk.rule.max-tac-prisoner-handling.combines: Local Hall of Justice or Security Facility

cyberpunk.rule.night-city-manager-author.name: Night City Manager authority

effect.summary: City Managers nominally oversee local services, infrastructure, zoning, licensing, and contracts; a mayor is only ceremonial.

cyberpunk.rule.night-city-manager-author.cost_or_limit: Combat Zone managers have little effective control over gangs.
cyberpunk.rule.night-city-manager-author.go_wrong: Factional conflict may undermine city authority.
cyberpunk.rule.night-city-manager-author.who_may: City Managers and Night City Council
cyberpunk.rule.night-city-manager-author.combines: Local Data Pool, zoning, taxes, licenses, contracts

cyberpunk.rule.bodyguard-use-of-force-li.name: Bodyguard use-of-force limit

effect.summary: Licensed personal guards may use maximum force only when their clients face immediate physical danger.

cyberpunk.rule.bodyguard-use-of-force-li.cost_or_limit: Maximum force requires immediate danger to the client.
cyberpunk.rule.bodyguard-use-of-force-li.go_wrong: Guards without arrest authority must call other forces to take prisoners.

cyberpunk.rule.uniform-civilian-justice-.name: Uniform Civilian Justice Code

effect.summary: It supplies the legal framework used in the United States and as the basis for Night City's laws.

cyberpunk.rule.uniform-civilian-justice-.cost_or_limit: Enforcement varies by location and income
cyberpunk.rule.uniform-civilian-justice-.combines: Follows the Military Justice Code period

cyberpunk.rule.military-justice-code.name: Military Justice Code

effect.summary: Military regulations replaced prior civilian law during martial law.

cyberpunk.rule.military-justice-code.cost_or_limit: Applied during a three-year martial-law period

cyberpunk.rule.corporate-cops-are-deputi.name: Corporate Cops are deputized to patrol only corporate facilities

effect.summary: Corporate police authority is limited to corporate premises.

cyberpunk.rule.corporate-cops-are-deputi.cost_or_limit: Dense office districts can effectively extend their patrol territory

cyberpunk.rule.theft-is-handled-by-the-v.name: Theft is handled by the victim on The Street

effect.summary: When theft is caught, the victim determines the punishment, ranging from a beating to killing.

cyberpunk.rule.theft-is-handled-by-the-v.go_wrong: Punishment may include torture or death

cyberpunk.rule.u-s-narcotics-possession-.name: U.S. narcotics possession restriction

effect.summary: none

cyberpunk.rule.u-s-narcotics-possession-.cost_or_limit: Narcotics possession is theoretically prohibited on U.S. premises; designer drugs classed as medicinal are excluded.
cyberpunk.rule.u-s-narcotics-possession-.combines: The passage says the rule has little practical force after most coca and opium plants were destroyed.
cyberpunk.rule.u-s-narcotics-possession-.blocked_reason: This is a world-law restriction, not a power effect.

cyberpunk.rule.exile-implant-city-code-r.name: Exile implant city-code rule

effect.summary: none

cyberpunk.rule.exile-implant-city-code-r.cost_or_limit: Each additional city offense can add a code; enough codes bar entry to civilization.
cyberpunk.rule.exile-implant-city-code-r.combines: The implant responds to a city phone NET transmission.
cyberpunk.rule.exile-implant-city-code-r.blocked_reason: This is a mechanism governing an implant's restrictions.

cyberpunk.rule.murder-death-penalty-and-.name: Murder death penalty and appeal

effect.summary: none

cyberpunk.rule.murder-death-penalty-and-.cost_or_limit: Death is standard for murder; new evidence may be produced during a three-month appeal.
cyberpunk.rule.murder-death-penalty-and-.blocked_reason: This is a legal procedure governing sentencing.

cyberpunk.rule.agency-connectivity-rule.name: Agency connectivity rule

effect.summary: none

cyberpunk.rule.agency-connectivity-rule.cost_or_limit: Online Agent functions require a provider; connectivity cost is included in Lifestyle.
cyberpunk.rule.agency-connectivity-rule.where_from: Distributed providers link wireless and existing network nodes.
cyberpunk.rule.agency-connectivity-rule.combines: No single company owns connectivity or all nodes.
cyberpunk.rule.agency-connectivity-rule.blocked_reason: This describes how network service is provided and paid for.

cyberpunk.rule.federal-weapons-statute-o.name: Federal Weapons Statute of 1999 identification liability

effect.summary: none

cyberpunk.rule.federal-weapons-statute-o.cost_or_limit: An owner is liable if their numbered gun is used in a crime, unless it was reported lost or stolen to local police beforehand.
cyberpunk.rule.federal-weapons-statute-o.who_may: Gun owners with an identifying weapon number.
cyberpunk.rule.federal-weapons-statute-o.combines: The serial number is cataloged with the weapon's ballistics pattern.
cyberpunk.rule.federal-weapons-statute-o.blocked_reason: This is a law assigning responsibility for a weapon's use.

cyberpunk.rule.federal-weapons-statute-o.name: Federal Weapons Statute of 1999 automatic-weapons restriction

effect.summary: none

cyberpunk.rule.federal-weapons-statute-o.cost_or_limit: Carrying submachine guns and other fully automatic weapons is illegal; possession brings a mandatory five-to-seven-year prison sentence.
cyberpunk.rule.federal-weapons-statute-o.who_may: People possessing or carrying restricted weapons.
cyberpunk.rule.federal-weapons-statute-o.blocked_reason: This is a legal restriction with a stated penalty.

cyberpunk.rule.ammunition-size-classes.name: Ammunition size classes

effect.summary: none

cyberpunk.rule.ammunition-size-classes.cost_or_limit: Modern guns generally use ammunition matched to gun size: Light, Medium, Heavy, or Very Heavy; rifles commonly use a standardized 7.62x39mm-based round.
cyberpunk.rule.ammunition-size-classes.combines: Local Techs can produce standardized rifle ammunition.
cyberpunk.rule.ammunition-size-classes.blocked_reason: This is a compatibility rule for weapons and ammunition.

cyberpunk.rule.data-pool-local-network-r.name: Data Pool local-network restriction

effect.summary: none

cyberpunk.rule.data-pool-local-network-r.cost_or_limit: Data Pools use limited city LANs in response to rampant NET sabotage; users generally need an account for their city's pool.
cyberpunk.rule.data-pool-local-network-r.combines: Each city operates its own version.
cyberpunk.rule.data-pool-local-network-r.blocked_reason: This is a world mechanism governing network reach and access.

cyberpunk.rule.night-market-access.name: Night Market access

effect.summary: Finding some markets requires personal connections or access codes.

cyberpunk.rule.night-market-access.cost_or_limit: Markets may be secret and temporary.
cyberpunk.rule.night-market-access.who_may: Those with the necessary connections or codes.
cyberpunk.rule.night-market-access.blocked_reason: This is a straightforward access restriction.

cyberpunk.rule.midnight-market-hosting.name: Midnight Market hosting

effect.summary: Only a Fixer of Rank 9 or higher can set up a Midnight Market.

cyberpunk.rule.midnight-market-hosting.blocked_reason: This is a straightforward rank restriction.

cyberpunk.rule.weapon-attachment-slots.name: Weapon attachment slots

effect.summary: Non-Exotic ranged weapons have three attachment slots; duplicate attachments do nothing and attachments must suit the weapon type.

cyberpunk.rule.weapon-attachment-slots.cost_or_limit: Each attachment occupies its slot cost; two attachments sharing physical space still charge their slots independently.
cyberpunk.rule.weapon-attachment-slots.blocked_reason: This is a straightforward equipment-slot restriction.

cyberpunk.rule.poor-quality-weapon.name: Poor Quality Weapon

effect.summary: A Critical Failure makes the weapon malfunction until the user spends an Action unjamming it.

cyberpunk.rule.poor-quality-weapon.cost_or_limit: Triggers on a roll of 1; clearing it requires an Action but no Check.
cyberpunk.rule.poor-quality-weapon.go_wrong: The weapon stops functioning until cleared.
cyberpunk.rule.poor-quality-weapon.combines: Applies to melee and ranged weapons.
cyberpunk.rule.poor-quality-weapon.blocked_reason: This is a simple triggered equipment failure.

cyberpunk.rule.excellent-quality-weapons.name: Excellent Quality Weapons

effect.summary: Adds +1 to the user’s attack check with the weapon.

cyberpunk.rule.excellent-quality-weapons.combines: Applies to melee and ranged attacks made with that weapon.
cyberpunk.rule.excellent-quality-weapons.blocked_reason: This is a simple numerical modifier.

cyberpunk.rule.sleep-deprivation-penalty.name: Sleep deprivation penalty

effect.summary: Going without six hours of sleep per day imposes -2 to attempts for each day since a full sleep.

cyberpunk.rule.sleep-deprivation-penalty.cost_or_limit: Applies for every day without six hours of sleep.
cyberpunk.rule.sleep-deprivation-penalty.who_may: Anyone who goes without the stated sleep
cyberpunk.rule.sleep-deprivation-penalty.blocked_reason: A numeric penalty can be applied directly.

cyberpunk.rule.uncomfortable-sleep-fatig.name: Uncomfortable sleep fatigue

effect.summary: Uncomfortable sleep causes fatigue the next day and an additional -2 to attempts.

cyberpunk.rule.uncomfortable-sleep-fatig.cost_or_limit: Cramming, street sleeping, or wilderness sleeping can qualify; street and wilderness sleep allow specified DV15 checks to avoid fatigue.
cyberpunk.rule.uncomfortable-sleep-fatig.who_may: Anyone sleeping in the described conditions

cyberpunk.rule.uncomfortable-sleep-fatig.blocked_reason: A next-day penalty is directly representable.

cyberpunk.rule.housing-occupancy-limit.name: Housing occupancy limit

effect.summary: Cramming means more occupants than one plus the number of bedrooms.

cyberpunk.rule.housing-occupancy-limit.cost_or_limit: People in cryostasis and corpses do not count; Cube Hotels use a special rule.
cyberpunk.rule.housing-occupancy-limit.go_wrong: Exceeding the limit makes sleep uncomfortable.
cyberpunk.rule.housing-occupancy-limit.combines: More than one person in a cube is always uncomfortable.
cyberpunk.rule.housing-occupancy-limit.blocked_reason: The rule is a direct numerical limit.

cyberpunk.rule.housing-eviction-and-star.name: Housing eviction and starvation priority

effect.summary: When forced to choose, being evicted is preferable to starving.

cyberpunk.rule.housing-eviction-and-star.blocked_reason: This is advice, not a mechanical effect.

cyberpunk.rule.hammock-weight-limit.name: Hammock weight limit

effect.summary: The tower hammocks cannot support someone with more than one cyberlimb.

cyberpunk.rule.hammock-weight-limit.cost_or_limit: More than one cyberlimb exceeds the stated limit.
cyberpunk.rule.hammock-weight-limit.go_wrong: The hammock will not support the occupant.

cyberpunk.rule.memory-ghost-sentience-di.name: Memory ghost sentience dispute

cyberpunk.rule.memory-ghost-sentience-di.where_from: Debate about data entities in the Old NET.
cyberpunk.rule.memory-ghost-sentience-di.combines: Relates to artificial intelligence and stored memories.

cyberpunk.rule.3d-printed-gun-failure.name: 3D-printed gun failure

cyberpunk.rule.3d-printed-gun-failure.cost_or_limit: The hazard applies to extremely cheap, unreliable printed weapons.
cyberpunk.rule.3d-printed-gun-failure.go_wrong: The weapon may explode during a firefight.
cyberpunk.rule.3d-printed-gun-failure.who_may: Users of cheaply printed guns are at risk.

cyberpunk.rule.law-of-the-broken-wheel.name: Law of the Broken Wheel

cyberpunk.rule.law-of-the-broken-wheel.cost_or_limit: Convoys, scavengers, and pirate Families are expected to avoid marked items.
cyberpunk.rule.law-of-the-broken-wheel.go_wrong: Violating the taboo can lead to exclusion from a convoy.
cyberpunk.rule.law-of-the-broken-wheel.who_may: Nomads follow it as an important cultural rule.
cyberpunk.rule.law-of-the-broken-wheel.where_from: A cultural warning tradition meant to survive societal collapse.
cyberpunk.rule.law-of-the-broken-wheel.combines: The atomic trefoil is taught as the Broken Wheel.

cyberpunk.rule.cyberoptic-option-limit.name: Cyberoptic option limit

effect.summary: A basic eye module can take up to four options per eye.

cyberpunk.rule.cyberoptic-option-limit.combines: Some equipment can provide additional mounting capacity.

cyberpunk.rule.gas-grenade-spread.name: Gas grenade spread

cyberpunk.rule.gas-grenade-spread.cost_or_limit: Three-metre initial range; dissipates by the third turn.

cyberpunk.rule.critical-patient-treatmen.name: Critical-patient treatment window

effect.summary: none stated

cyberpunk.rule.critical-patient-treatmen.cost_or_limit: The damaged text refers to checks and treatment over successive days, but the exact mechanism is not recoverable.

cyberpunk.rule.corporate-stock-voting.name: Corporate stock voting

effect.summary: none stated

cyberpunk.rule.corporate-stock-voting.cost_or_limit: A controlling majority vote can direct company decisions; greater share ownership brings greater control.
cyberpunk.rule.corporate-stock-voting.combines: Shares can be traded and sold as corporate assets.
